solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Revamped Saudi PVC and international rubber business

indicators.note: something revamped has been remade, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Saudi plastics company and a global rubber firm get a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: PVC and 'rubber business' suggest industry, but a rubber is a match in this tennis competition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davis Cup is the international men's tennis team event, whose individual matches are called rubbers.

clue.text: Of the fifty US states, ten finally earn a mention of sorts

parts.note: all fifty states together are all of the US
ten written as the digits 1 and 0

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: last letter of earn

explanation.surface: Of all the US states, a mere ten get any sort of reference.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference, so it is a kind of mention.

clue.text: Note what you're hoping to work out, after sort of light hesitation

indicators.note: after says the note and the solution come second, so the light abbreviation leads the answer

parts.note: infrared, a sort of light
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

parts.words: what you're hoping to work out
parts.note: the answer to a puzzle is what you hope to work out

explanation.surface: A solver hesitates over a glimmer of an idea before hoping to crack the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the light piece first; the note and the solution follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Irresolution is indecision, a failure to make up one's mind, which is hesitation.

clue.text: Had races organised as party game

indicators.note: organising things puts them in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At a party, the guests held organised races as their game.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a parlour game in which players mime words for others to guess.

clue.text: Hell for quiet supporter of mine!

parts.note: the pit is hell, the bottomless pit
pro means in favour of, for
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An exclamation from someone who backs a mine wanting peace: Hell!
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word, but it supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit prop is a timber or steel post that holds up the roof of a mine.

clue.text: Husband effectively to provide this plant?

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the noun for doing it
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to husband resources is to manage them carefully and economically
second meaning: a pink-flowered seaside plant, also called sea pink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like a spouse, but here it is the verb meaning to economise.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift is careful economy with money, and also the name of a coastal flowering plant.

clue.text: Bed you'll find in Washington DC's superior

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
a Detective Inspector ranks above a Detective Constable

explanation.surface: A bed found in a grand building in the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington DC' reads as the city, but DC is a police rank, Detective Constable.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry river bed in desert regions that fills only after rain.

clue.text: One rolling up for protection from fellow corporate head: what a blunder!

parts.note: a fellow is a he
Director General, head of the BBC, known as the Corporation
eh? asks someone to repeat, like what?
an own goal, a blunder in football

explanation.surface: A company boss seeks cover after a colleague makes a costly mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for protection' looks like part of the wordplay, but it ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgehog curls into a spiny ball when threatened, rolling itself up as a defence.

clue.text: Cruel, having daft host do a tune!

indicators.note: a host takes in guests, so the word for daft holds the tune phrase inside it

parts.note: inane means silly or daft
to hum is to produce a tune with closed lips

explanation.surface: Someone finds it cruel to be made to sing by a silly host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' looks like the person making demands, but it only signals that one piece holds the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane describes behaviour lacking compassion, the same as cruel.

clue.text: Something indistinct posh sort of camera conceals

indicators.note: what conceals something keeps it inside, so the camera letters wrap round the posh letter

parts.note: a single-lens reflex camera
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A smart camera fails to hide something blurry in the picture.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside SLR to give S-U-LR.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is an indistinct, run-together sound in speech or music.

clue.text: Deafening activity in cornmill?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a gerund sense; the answer itself is an adjective
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: breaking up ears of corn

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a mill dealing with ears of corn. Strictly a mill grinds rather than splits them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so loud it seems to split the ears is a common idiom for a deafening noise.

clue.text: Thursday elevenses — small, not large — including a whole lot of water

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so the built word holds the article
says a small-size letter replaces a large-size one, as on clothing labels

parts.note: TH is the abbreviation for Thursday
a mid-morning snack, eaten about eleven o'clock
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Thursday mid-morning snack, scaled down, is taken with plenty of water.
explanation.walkthrough: S for small replaces L for large in ELEVENSES, giving ESEVENSES; A then goes in before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: The seven seas is the traditional phrase for all the world's oceans, a huge quantity of water.

clue.text: Entrance to basilica provided with ancient sort of doors?

indicators.note: the entrance is the way in, so only the opening letter of the church word is kept

parts.note: first letter of basilica
provided that means on condition, i.e. if
ancient means old

explanation.surface: The church's entrance was fitted with doors of an antique kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifold doors fold in two panels; bifold is used as an adjective for that type of door.

clue.text: Welfare initiative with intent: right for everyone

parts.note: out as in 'out to win', set on a goal
R is the abbreviation for right
as in 'five pounds each', a price for everyone

explanation.surface: A charity scheme pursued with determination, meant to be right for all.
explanation.definitionFit: Outreach is community work by an organisation that takes its services to people in need.

clue.text: Pain keeping yours truly in old Scottish county hospital

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the county name holds the self-referring letter

parts.note: Angus is a former Scottish county
yours truly is the setter, who says I
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone in pain is kept in a hospital in an old Scottish county.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside ANGUS before its last letter, and H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe suffering, mental or physical, so it works as a synonym for pain.

clue.text: Militant part of drama to be played out much earlier?

parts.note: Act IV, a late section of a five-act play

parts.words: to be played out much earlier?
parts.note: 1st, i.e. first, a placing long before the fourth

explanation.surface: A campaigner's role in a play was meant to be performed far sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers a loose hint: Act IV, then 1ST written with I for the digit, the first act coming much earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: An activist campaigns vigorously for a cause, as does a militant.

clue.text: Test position pontiff, inelegantly, has adopted

indicators.note: what is adopted is taken in, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: The pope has awkwardly taken up a stance in a trial of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; fine leg is a fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine leg is a fielding position in cricket, so it is a place a fielder takes in a Test match.

clue.text: Acting style by lead on paper better

definitions.note: an adjective sense, as in improved health

parts.note: improv is improvised theatre
the editor leads a newspaper

explanation.surface: An actor's style, judged by the leading role in a newspaper review, got better.
explanation.definitionFit: Something improved has been made better than before, so improved and better are synonyms.

clue.text: Point to angle being formed, as protractors do?

parts.note: east, a compass point

indicators.note: being formed means being shaped anew, so these letters are moulded into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pointing to an angle being made, as a geometry instrument does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protractors' looks like the geometry tool, but here it means people who protract, i.e. draw things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract something is to lengthen it, so protractors are things or people that elongate.

clue.text: Films covering game seen in winter sports venues

indicators.note: a covering goes over something, so the films word wraps around the game

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or layer
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Movies about a match shown where people go for winter sports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' reads as movies, but it means thin layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski runs are slopes laid out for skiing, the venues for that winter sport.

clue.text: With team not qualified, we're obliged to find station for lift home?

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
a team of eleven, as in cricket or football
rank as in 'rank outsider', utter, unqualified

explanation.surface: The team didn't qualify, so the players must find a ride home.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface order is TA, then 'with team' adds XI, then RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi rank is a place where cabs wait, a station from which one can get a lift home.

clue.text: Batting team ultimately so determined?

definitions.note: describes the side's final state rather than naming a thing
definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket a side whose batters are all dismissed is ...

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the batting side's innings ends when ten batters are dismissed and the team is all out.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-out effort is total and determined, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Disinfectant no help with dislocation

indicators.note: a dislocated joint is knocked out of place, so these letters are moved out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A disinfectant is useless when someone has a dislocated joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenol, also called carbolic acid, was the early antiseptic used to disinfect wounds and surfaces.

clue.text: Several guards in front of gatehouse look cocky

indicators.note: guards stand around what they protect, so the outer word surrounds the rest

parts.note: various means several
taken as written

indicators.note: the front is the start, so just the opening letter of the building word is used

parts.note: first letter of gatehouse
lo is an old word meaning look!

explanation.surface: Several sentries by a gatehouse appear full of swagger.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or behold, as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglorious means boastful and proud of oneself, which is what cocky describes.

clue.text: One's always gracious

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) becomes I's
ay (or aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Someone is always courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' looks like courteous, but it is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, so one can stand in for the other.

clue.text: Dash from Channel, moving east to west

indicators.note: on a map east is the right-hand end and west the left, so the last letter goes to the start

parts.note: a lane is a channel, as in a shipping lane

explanation.surface: A quick crossing of the English Channel, heading from France to England.
explanation.walkthrough: E is both the last letter of LANE and the abbreviation for east; it moves from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan and dash both mean flair and vigorous style.

clue.text: Found vase for leading performer

parts.note: to found something is to start it
an urn is a type of vase

explanation.surface: Someone has discovered a vase that will serve the headline act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: A star turn is the main act in a show, the performer who tops the bill.

clue.text: Bypass that is expanded in Home Counties, with parking

indicators.note: in places one thing within another, so the region's letters go round the Latin phrase

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England
i.e. written out in full is the Latin id est
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A road bypass in the commuter belt around London, with car parking, has been enlarged.
explanation.walkthrough: ID EST goes inside SE, then P follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a problem is to avoid it by going round, i.e. to bypass it.
